subject: Request: executive authorization for MerchantCare Hosted API rate concession (>20%)
messages:
From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@merchantcare.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal and terms

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the proposal — MerchantCare is excited about Redwood's latency and cost profile. I reviewed the numbers with our finance team and we're constrained by a Q3 budget cap. To move forward with a signed commitment for the pilot and rollout, we need a deeper first-year concession. Specifically: a 30% discount on hosted API usage for the first 12 months in exchange for a committed 12-month spend of $150,000 (prepaid or monthly payments).

Our rationale: we can commit to a tightly scoped integration and be a reference customer for the healthcare vertical in exchange for the concession. If Redwood can greenlight this, procurement will prioritize the contract and we can aim to sign within two weeks.

Attachments: MerchantCare_SOW_v2.pdf, MC_usage_forecast_Q3-Q4.xlsx

Regards,
Sara Lin
Head of Product
MerchantCare Inc
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: MerchantCare request - asking for exec approval (>20%)

Team,

Forwarding MerchantCare's ask — they want 30% off Hosted API for 12 months against a $150k commit. They're offering a reference and expedited procurement if we can commit quickly. Quick summary of commercials and rationale:
- Baseline list rate expected revenue: ~$214k ARR on their usage profile (per attachment).
- Proposed concession: 30% first-year discount -> implied $150k first-year commit per customer ask.
- Upside: reference in healthcare vertical, potential expansion into multi-region pilot in H1 2028.

Ask: we need exec authorization for anything >20%. Can you run margin impact and legal constraints, and advise a recommended authorization? If we can't do 30% straight, consider structured concession (deeper initial discount + ramp).

I've cc'd David for visibility.

Ben
Account Exec — Strategic Health
Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — quick initial thoughts:

1) Deal hygiene: need proper SOW boundaries (they attached one but it's light on token caps and retention). Legal to review.
2) Pricing options: rather than flat 30% for 12 months, suggest one of the following structures we can present to the customer:
   - Option A: 30% off for first 3 months while they validate, then step to 15% for months 4-12.
   - Option B: 25% off for the full 12 months with a $150k committed spend (safer on margin).
   - Option C: 30% off with prepayment + 6% non-refundable onboarding credit to offset churn risk.

3) Strategic signal: MerchantCare is a good reference for healthcare. I would be comfortable recommending up to 25% as an exec sign-off with finance guardrails and a prepayment or milestone-based credit. Anything above 25% should come with stronger protections (prepayment, caps, or a shorter deep discount window).

Karthik, can you run the modeled unit economics and confirm the steady-state margin at both 25% and 30%? Mina, can you weigh in on finance guardrails and recommended billing terms?

-Marissa
Director, Deal Desk
Redwood Inference

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-02T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MerchantCare pricing request — finance assessment

Couple data points from finance after reviewing the forecast (MC_usage_forecast_Q3-Q4.xlsx):
- Expected monthly token volume (pilot): ~40M tokens/month initially, ramping to ~160M tokens/month by month 9 if adoption goes well.
- With current kernel selections and expected batching we estimate cost-in-use at ~0.012 USD/token-equivalent (model + infra blended).
- At a 30% list-rate concession across the board, first-year gross margin would be low (~12%), which is below our typical target for new strategic pilots. 25% generates roughly ~20% gross margin with the $150k committed guarantee — that's acceptable provided we secure prepayment or equivalent protection.

Recommended guardrails:
- Prepayment for first 6 months or an irrevocable monthly ACH for the full year.
- Token cap in SOW with overage terms billed at list less 10% (not the discounted rate).
- Milestone: reference + case study sign-off by MerchantCare product team within 6 months to unlock the remaining discounted tranche.

If the leadership wants to approve 30%, I recommend we: require prepayment, set an initial 3-month deep discount window, and include clear overage billing at list less 10%.

-Mina
VP, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-03T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MerchantCare request - executive authorization

Appreciate the analysis and options. After weighing strategic value and finance recommendations, I authorize a one-time executive concession of 25% off Hosted API usage for MerchantCare for 12 months, subject to the following conditions (must be in SOW/Order Form):

1) Customer signs a 12-month commitment for $150,000 (minimum guaranteed).
2) Prepayment for the first 6 months is required or monthly ACH with an irrevocable payment guarantee.
3) SOW must include a token cap for billed usage. Any usage above the cap will be billed at list price minus 10% (no retroactive application of the 25%).
4) Customer must agree to be a public reference and participate in a short case study within 6 months; failure to do so converts the remaining discount to 10% for months 7-12.
5) Legal to finalize limited liability language and standard privacy clauses; retention and PHI handling must be explicitly documented in SOW.

This approval is for 25% (which exceeds the 20% delegated threshold) and is conditioned on the above. Ben — please move to legal and procurement and close the loop. If MerchantCare insists on 30% flat, escalate back to me with a churn/termination plan and counter-structure.

-David
David Kim
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
